title: Power Round — 2013 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1a (1 pt). Statement: 1a. Compute d(6), d(16), and d(72).

criteria.name: Problem 1b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1b (2 pts). Statement: 1b. Of the houses with positive numbers less than 100, ﬁnd, with proof, the house or houses which is (are) closest to City Hall.

criteria.name: Problem 1c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1c (1 pt). Statement: 1c. Find four houses at a distance of 1 /9 from house number 17.

criteria.name: Problem 1d
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1d (2 pts). Statement: 1d. Find an inﬁnite sequence of houses {hn} such that d(17,h 1)>d (17,h 2)>··· >d (17,hn)>d (17,hn+1)>··· .

criteria.name: Problem 2a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2a (1 pt). Statement: 2a. Find four houses in N (6).

criteria.name: Problem 2b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2b (1 pt). Statement: 2b. Suppose that n is a house with d(n) = 1. Find four houses in N (n).

criteria.name: Problem 2c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2c (2 pts). Statement: 2c. Suppose that n is a house with d(n) = 1/27. Determine the ten smallest positive integers m (in the standard ordering of the integers) such that m∈N (n).

criteria.name: Problem 3a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3a (1 pt). Statement: 3a. Notice that d(16) = d(17) = 1 and that d(16, 17) = 1. Is it true that, for all m,n such that d(m) =d(n) = 1 andm̸=n,d(m,n ) = 1? Either prove your answer or ﬁnd a counterexample.

criteria.name: Problem 3b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3b (2 pts). Statement: 3b. Suppose that d(m) =d(n) = 1/3k and that m̸=n. Determine the possible values of d(m,n ).

criteria.name: Problem 3c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3c (2 pts). Statement: 3c. Suppose that d(17,m ) = 1/81. Determine the possible values of d(16,m ).

criteria.name: Problem 4a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4a (1 pt). Statement: 4a. Show that d(17, 51)≤d(17, 34) +d(34, 51) and that d(17, 95)≤d(17, 68) +d(68, 95).

criteria.name: Problem 4b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4b (2 pts). Statement: 4b. If a = 17 and b = 68, determine all values of c such that d(a,c ) =d(a,b ).

criteria.name: Problem 5a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5a (2 pts). Statement: 5a. Prove that, for all a and b, d(a,b )≤ max{d(a),d (b)}.

criteria.name: Problem 5b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5b (2 pts). Statement: 5b. Prove that, for all a, b, and c, d(a,c )≤ max{d(a,b ),d (b,c )}.

criteria.name: Problem 5c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5c (1 pt). Statement: 5c. Prove that, for all a, b, and c, d(a,c )≤d(a,b ) +d(b,c ).

criteria.name: Problem 5d
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5d (2 pts). Statement: 5d. After thinking about it some more, the visitor announces that all ARMLopolitan triangles have a special property. What is it? Justify your answer.

criteria.name: Problem 6a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6a (1 pt). Statement: 6a. Find at least one house whose distance from City Hall changes as a result of the move.

criteria.name: Problem 6b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6b (2 pts). Statement: 6b. Prove that the distance between houses with consecutive numbers does not change after the move.

criteria.name: Problem 7a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7a (2 pts). Statement: 7a. The residents of N (1) value their suburban location and protest the move, claiming it will make them closer to City Hall. Will it? Justify your answer.

criteria.name: Problem 7b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7b (2 pts). Statement: 7b. Some residents ofN (9) claim that their tightly-knit community will be disrupted by the move: they will be scattered between diﬀerent neighborhoods after the change. Will they? Justify your answer.

criteria.name: Problem 7c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7c (2 pts). Statement: 7c. Other residents ofN (9) claim that their community will be disrupted by newcomers: they say that after the move, their new neighborhood will also contain residents previously from several diﬀerent old neighborhoods (not just the new arrivals to ARMLopolis). Will it? Justify your answer.

criteria.name: Problem 7d
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7d (2 pts). Statement: 7d. Determine all values of n such thatN (n) will either entirely relocate (i.e., all residents r of N (n) are at a diﬀerent distance from City Hall than they were before), lose residents (as in 7b), or gain residents besides the new ARMLopolitans (as in 7c).

criteria.name: Problem 8a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8a (2 pts). Statement: 8a. One day, Paul (house 23) and Sally (house 32), longtime residents of N (1), are discussing the “2 side” of the neighborhood, that is, the set of houses {n|n = 3k + 2, k∈ Z}. Paul says “I feel like I’m at the center of the “2 side”: when I looked out my window, I realized that the “2 side” consists of exactly those houses whose distance from me is at most 1 /3.” Prove that Paul is correct.

criteria.name: Problem 8b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8b (2 pts). Statement: 8b. Sally replies “It’s not all about you: I have the same experience!” Justify Sally’s claim; in other words, prove that {n| n = 3k + 2, k∈ Z} consists exactly of those houses whose distance from Sally’s house is at most 1 /3.

criteria.name: Problem 8c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8c (2 pts). Statement: 8c. Paul’s and Sally’s observations can be generalized. For any x, letDr(x) ={y|d(x,y )≤r}, that is,Dr(x) is the disk of radius r. Prove that if d(x,z ) =r, thenDr(x) =Dr(z).

criteria.name: Problem 9a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9a (2 pts). Statement: 9a. Ross takes a walk starting at his house, which is number 34. He ﬁrst visits house n1, such that d(n1, 34) = 1/3. He then goes to another house, n2, such that d(n1,n 2) = 1/3. Continuing in that way, he visits houses n3,n 4,..., and each time, d(ni,ni+1) = 1/3. At the end of the day, what is his maximum possible distance from his original house? Justify your answer.

criteria.name: Problem 9b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9b (2 pts). Statement: 9b. Generalize your answer to 9a: given a value of n0, determine the rational values ofr for which the sequence n1,n 2,... with d(ni,ni+1) = r is entirely contained in a circle of ﬁnite radius centered at n0.

criteria.name: Problem 10a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10a (1 pt). Statement: 10a. Compute d(3/5),d (5/8), and d(7/18).

criteria.name: Problem 10b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10b (1 pt). Statement: 10b. Determine all pairs of relatively prime integers p and q such that p/q∈N (4/3).

criteria.name: Problem 10c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10c (2 pts). Statement: s same address. When asked, he says “My old address was e, that is, the sum 1 0! + 1 1! + 1 2! +... . I’d really like to keep that address, because the addresses of my friends here are all partial sums of this series: Alice’s house is 1 0!, Bob’s house is 1 0! + 1 1!, Carol’s house is 1 0! + 1 1! + 1 2!, and so on. Just let me know what I have to do in order to be near my friends!” After some head-scratching, the ARMLopolitan planning council announces that this request cannot be satisﬁed: there is no number, rational or otherwise, that corresponds to the (inﬁnite) sum, or that is arbitrarily close to the houses in this sequence. Prove that the council is correct (and not just bureaucratic).
